---
name: 'build container images'

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
      - main
    tags:
      - '*'

jobs:
  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Prepare
        id: prep
        run: |
          DOCKER_IMAGE=quay.io/mudler/luet-k8s-controller
          VERSION=latest
          SHORTREF=${GITHUB_SHA::8}

          # If this is git tag, use the tag name as a docker tag
          if [[ $GITHUB_REF == refs/tags/* ]]; then
            VERSION=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
          fi
          TAGS="${DOCKER_IMAGE}:${VERSION},${DOCKER_IMAGE}:${SHORTREF}"

          # If the VERSION looks like a version number, assume that
          # this is the most recent version of the image and also
          # tag it 'latest'.
          #if [[ $VERSION =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}$ ]]; then
            TAGS="$TAGS,${DOCKER_IMAGE}:latest"
          #fi

          # Set output parameters.
          echo ::set-output name=tags::${TAGS}
          echo ::set-output name=docker_image::${DOCKER_IMAGE}

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@master
        with:
          platforms: all

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        id: buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@master

      - name: Login to DockerHub
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v1
        with:
          registry: quay.io
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_RELEASE_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_RELEASE_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v2
        with:
          builder: ${{ steps.buildx.outputs.name }}
          context: .
          file: ./Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.prep.outputs.tags }}

# buildah Backend Migration — Design (Spec C)

Date: 2026-07-21
Status: Approved, pending implementation plan
Branch: `spec-c-buildah-backend`

## Problem

luet is replacing the unmaintained `genuinetools/img` build backend with
buildah ([luet#391](https://github.com/mudler/luet/pull/391)). img has been
effectively unmaintained since 2018 and the version this project installs was
released in 2020.

This controller requests `img` explicitly: `factory.go` defines an `ImgBackend`
constant, passes it to `luet build --backend`, and `types.go` returns it as the
default when a `PackageBuild` does not specify one. So `img` is not an opt-in
here, it is the path every build takes unless overridden.

luet retains `--backend img` as a deprecated alias resolving to buildah, which
means the *flag* this controller passes keeps working. Two things are not
covered by that alias:

1. The alias resolves to the buildah backend, which then **execs the `buildah`
   binary**. The controller image must contain it.
2. `factory.go` prepends `img login` as a raw binary invocation in a shell
   string when registry credentials are enabled. luet never sees that command,
   so no aliasing can rewrite it.

## Prerequisite

The controller image must ship buildah. That is a separate, already-verified
change on the `bump-base-buildah` branch: it moves the base from
`ubuntu:20.04` to `ubuntu:24.04` and installs buildah alongside img.

buildah is not installable on ubuntu 20.04 at all. It is absent from main and
universe, and mocaccinoOS has no buildah package, so the `luet install
container/...` route used for img is unavailable. 22.04 offers buildah 1.23.1,
exactly the release where `buildah bud` became `buildah build`; 24.04 offers
1.33.7, which is what the luet backend was developed and tested against.

**This spec assumes that change has landed.** Implementing it against the
current image produces a controller that requests a binary the image does not
have.

## Scope

In scope: the controller changes that make buildah the backend it requests and
that give rootless buildah the environment it needs.

Out of scope: the Dockerfile change (prerequisite above), and any change to
luet itself.

## Backend selection

`factory.go:14-18` gains a fourth constant alongside the existing three:

```go
BuildahBackend = "buildah"
```

`types.go:102` changes its default from `"img"` to `"buildah"`, so existing
`PackageBuild` resources that do not name a backend move to buildah.

`img` remains an accepted explicit value. luet's deprecated alias resolves it
to buildah, so a resource naming it continues to work during the transition.
It is not rejected, and the constant is not removed.

### `img` must be treated as buildah everywhere, not just passed through

This is the subtle part of the change, and getting it wrong produces a
configuration that looks correct and fails at runtime.

When a resource names `img` explicitly, the controller passes `--backend img`
and **luet runs buildah**. So from the pod's point of view that build is a
buildah build: it needs the buildah environment variables and, with credentials
enabled, a `buildah login` rather than an `img login`. Keying those off the
literal string `"buildah"` alone would leave explicit-`img` resources running
buildah without its environment and attempting to log in with a binary whose
backend is no longer in use.

Every decision downstream of backend selection therefore keys off a single
helper rather than comparing strings ad hoc:

```go
// usesBuildah reports whether luet will run the buildah backend for this
// build. luet resolves the deprecated "img" backend to buildah, so both
// values mean buildah from the pod's point of view.
func usesBuildah(backend string) bool {
    return backend == BuildahBackend || backend == ImgBackend
}
```

The registry-login switch, the environment variables, and any future
buildah-conditional behavior all use it. The `--backend` argument itself is
unaffected: it keeps passing whatever the resource asked for, so luet emits its
own deprecation warning for `img` and the user learns to migrate.

## Registry login

`factory.go:133` and `factory.go:230` each prepend a login command when
`packageBuild.Spec.RegistryCredentials.Enabled`. Both switch on the backend and
both need to prepend `buildah login` whenever `usesBuildah(...)` is true,
taking the same `-u` / `-p` / URI arguments as the existing img case. Because
`img` now means buildah, the existing `case ImgBackend:` arm is replaced rather
than sitting alongside a new one: leaving it would emit `img login` for a build
that runs buildah.

Both sites matter. They are separate functions building separate commands, and
missing one produces a credentialed build that fails at push time with an
authentication error rather than anything that points at the backend.

## Rootless environment

Rootless buildah needs two environment variables, appended to the container
environment alongside the existing `TMPDIR` and `USER` entries
(`factory.go:342` onward):

- `BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot` — the default `runc` isolation does not work
  rootless.
- `STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` — overlay-on-overlay generally fails inside a pod
  without `/dev/fuse`.

Both are set only when `usesBuildah(...)` is true, so explicit-`img`
resources get them too. The docker and docker-sidecar backends must not
inherit them.

`vfs` is materially slower than `overlay`, particularly for large images. That
cost is accepted here and is already recorded in luet's own buildah design.
Where a cluster permits exposing `/dev/fuse`, buildah can use `fuse-overlayfs`
instead, but that is not something this controller configures.

## Seccomp

`factory.go:339-340` already sets apparmor and seccomp to unconfined, via
annotations, with the comment "Needed by img":

```go
podAnnotations["container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/spec-build"] = "unconfined"
podAnnotations["container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/spec-build"] = "unconfined"
```

The seccomp annotation form was deprecated in Kubernetes 1.19 and **removed in
1.25**, so on any cluster at 1.25 or newer that line has no effect. The
apparmor annotation was deprecated in 1.30 and still functions.

This matters because rootless buildah calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, which a
default seccomp profile blocks. Verified directly: under a default profile
buildah fails with `Error during unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER): Operation not
permitted`; with the profile unconfined the same build succeeds.

The container `SecurityContext` therefore gains the GA field, while the
annotations are retained for clusters older than 1.19:

```go
SecurityContext: &corev1.SecurityContext{
    RunAsUser:  &secUID,
    ProcMount:  &pmount,
    Privileged: &privileged,
    SeccompProfile: &corev1.SeccompProfile{
        Type: corev1.SeccompProfileTypeUnconfined,
    },
},
```

The comment above the annotations should be updated: the reason is no longer
img, it is rootless buildah's user-namespace call.

## No capability changes

An earlier draft of this work claimed rootless buildah needs `SETUID` and
`SETGID` granted explicitly. That is wrong, and testing showed it: a rootless
`buildah build` succeeded as uid 1000 with no capability additions at all,
because both capabilities are already in the default set. Adding them would be
cargo-culting, so this design does not.

## Verification status

Verified by building the `bump-base-buildah` image and running it:

- `uid=1000(luet)`, not the stock ubuntu user 24.04 ships on that uid
- buildah 1.33.7 and img 0.5.11 both present
- `cap_setuid` / `cap_setgid` preserved on `newuidmap` / `newgidmap`, setuid
  bits still stripped
- subuid and subgid ranges allocated for `luet` (100000:65536), which rootless
  mapping depends on
- a rootless `buildah build` as uid 1000 succeeds, and its output reads back

Not verified, and this is the main risk:

- **None of this has run in an actual Kubernetes pod.** The testing above used
  a Docker container, which approximates a pod but is not one. kubelet applies
  its own seccomp and apparmor defaults, and `UnmaskedProcMount` requires a
  permissive Pod Security Standard or PodSecurityPolicy.
- The Kubernetes version at which the alpha seccomp annotation stopped working
  (1.25) is taken from upstream documentation, not tested here.

Closing that gap requires a cluster and cannot be done from the repository.

## Testing

`factory.go` has no test file today. Two layers are appropriate:

1. **Table-driven unit tests over the generated pod spec.** Given a
   `PackageBuild`, assert the `--backend` argument, the presence and shape of
   the `buildah login` prefix when credentials are enabled, the two environment
   variables, that the docker backends do *not* receive them, and that
   `SeccompProfile` is set. The table must cover an explicit `backend: img`
   resource and assert it gets the buildah environment and `buildah login`,
   since that is the case most easily got wrong. These are pure functions over a struct, so they
   need no cluster and run in milliseconds.

2. **Manual verification on a real cluster.** Only this proves the rootless
   build actually runs. The unit tests cover the wiring; they cannot cover
   kubelet's behavior.

The unit tests are the deliverable here. The cluster check is a release gate,
recorded so it is not mistaken for something the tests already do.

## Risk

The largest risk is that the pod-level security configuration is correct in
principle but rejected or overridden by a given cluster's Pod Security
Standards. `UnmaskedProcMount` and an unconfined seccomp profile are both
privileged-ish settings that a restrictive namespace will refuse. That is not
introduced by this change, since the pod already requests both, but the
migration makes seccomp genuinely load-bearing where previously the setting was
inert on modern clusters and img evidently coped.

In other words: this change may surface an existing misconfiguration rather
than cause a new one.

import (
	corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"

)

// +genclient
// +k8s:deepcopy-gen:interfaces=k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime.Object

// PackageBuild is a specification for a PackageBuild resource
type PackageBuild struct {
	metav1.TypeMeta   `json:",inline"`
	metav1.ObjectMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`

	Spec   BuildSpec   `json:"spec"`
	Status BuildStatus `json:"status"`
}

// +genclient
// +k8s:deepcopy-gen:interfaces=k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime.Object

// RepoBuild is a specification for a RepoBuild resource

	metav1.TypeMeta   `json:",inline"`
	metav1.ObjectMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`

	Spec   RepoBuildSpec   `json:"spec"`
	Status RepoBuildStatus `json:"status"`
}

type Storage struct {
	Enabled    bool   `json:"enabled"`
	APIURL     string `json:"url"`
	SecretKey  string `json:"secretKey"`
	AccessID   string `json:"accessID"`
	Bucket     string `json:"bucket"`
	Path       string `json:"path"`
	FromSecret string `json:"fromSecret"`
}

type BuildOptions struct {
	Color   bool     `json:"color"`
	Spinner bool     `json:"spinner"`
	Values  []string `json:"values"`

	Emoji bool `json:"emoji"`

	Full bool `json:"full"`

	Retry int `json:"retry"`

	Env []corev1.EnvVar `json:"environment"`

	Backend string `json:"backend"`

	Pull       bool     `json:"pull"`
	OnlyTarget bool     `json:"onlyTarget"`
	NoDeps     bool     `json:"noDeps"`
	Tree       []string `json:"tree"`
	Debug      bool     `json:"debug"`

	Push bool `json:"push"`
	// --push-final-images
	PushFinalImages bool `json:"pushFinalImages"`
	// --push-final-images-force
	PushFinalImagesWithForce bool `json:"forcePushFinalImages"`
	// --push-final-images-repository
	FinalImagesRepository string `json:"finalImagesRepository"`

	PullRepository []string `json:"pullRepository"`

	ImageRepository string                      `json:"imageRepository"`
	Compression     string                      `json:"compression"`
	Privileged      bool                        `json:"privileged"`
	Resources       corev1.ResourceRequirements `json:"resources"`
}

func (b BuildOptions) GetBackend() string {
	if b.Backend == "docker-sidecar" {
		return "docker"
	}
	if b.Backend == "" {
		return "buildah"
	}
	return b.Backend
}

type CreateRepositoryOptions struct {
	Enabled         bool     `json:"enabled"`
	Type            string   `json:"type"`
	Urls            []string `json:"urls"`
	TreeCompression string   `json:"treeCompression"`

	MetaCompression string `json:"metaCompression"`
	MetaFileName    string `json:"metaFileName"`

	PushImages  bool   `json:"pushImages"`

	Description string `json:"description"`
	Name        string `json:"name"`
	OutputImage string `json:"image"`
}

type RegistryCredentials struct {
	Enabled    bool   `json:"enabled"`
	Registry   string `json:"registry"` // e.g. quay.io
	Username   string `json:"username"`
	Password   string `json:"password"`
	FromSecret string `json:"fromSecret"`
}

type Repository struct {
	Url      string `json:"url"`
	Path     string `json:"path"`
	Checkout string `json:"checkout"`
}

// BuildSpec is the spec for a PackageBuild resource
type BuildSpec struct {
	PackageName         string                  `json:"packageName"`
	Packages            []string                `json:"packages"`
	Repository          Repository              `json:"repository"`
	Storage             Storage                 `json:"storage"`
	Options             BuildOptions            `json:"options"`
	RegistryCredentials RegistryCredentials     `json:"registry"`
	NodeSelector        map[string]string       `json:"nodeSelector"`
	Annotations         map[string]string       `json:"annotations"`
	Labels              map[string]string       `json:"labels"`
	LuetRepository      CreateRepositoryOptions `json:"luetRepository"`

	WaitFor []string `json:"waitFor"`

	PodScheduler string `json:"podScheduler"`
}

type RepoBuildSpec struct {
	Packages      []string       `json:"packages"`
	Repository    LuetRepository `json:"repository"`
	GitRepository Repository     `json:"git_repository"`

	// Those belows will populate packagebuilds generated
	Storage             Storage                 `json:"storage"`
	Options             BuildOptions            `json:"options"`
	RegistryCredentials RegistryCredentials     `json:"registry"`
	NodeSelector        map[string]string       `json:"nodeSelector"`
	Annotations         map[string]string       `json:"annotations"`
	Labels              map[string]string       `json:"labels"`
	LuetRepository      CreateRepositoryOptions `json:"luetRepository"`

	PodScheduler string `json:"podScheduler"`
}

type LuetRepository struct {
	Name        string   `json:"name"`
	Description string   `json:"description"`
	Urls        []string `json:"urls"`
	Type        string   `json:"type"`
}

type BuildStatus struct {
	State string `json:"state"`
	Retry int    `json:"retry"`
	Node  string `json:"node"`
}

type RepoBuildStatus struct {
	State     string `json:"state"`
	BuildTree string `json:"buildtree"`
	Computed  bool   `json:"computed"`
}

# (experimental) Luet Kubernetes CRD controller

Simple CRD that uses [luet](https://github.com/mudler/luet) and [buildah](https://buildah.io) to build packages on Kubernetes. It doesn't require `privileged` permissions, and builds the image as user `1000` in the workload pod.

If you need to build docker images only, have a look at [img-controller](https://github.com/mudler/img-controller/)

## Install

To install it in your k8s cluster:

```bash
$ kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mudler/luet-k8s/master/hack/kube.yaml
```

## Build packages

The controller expose a new `PackageBuild` Kubernetes resource type, which can be used to build docker images with `buildah` and packages with `luet`.

To build a package, for example:

```bash

$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: build.luet.io/v1alpha1
kind: PackageBuild
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  packageName: container/img
  repository: 
    url: "https://github.com/mocaccinoOS/mocaccino-extra"
  options:
    pull: true
    imageRepository: "quay.io/mocaccinocache/extra-amd64-cache"
EOF
```


### Full example


```yaml
apiVersion: build.luet.io/v1alpha1
kind: PackageBuild
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  annotations:
    # Annotations to apply to workload pod
  labels:
    # Labels to apply to workload pod
  nodeSelector:
    # node Selector labels
  packageName: container/img
  registry:
    enabled: true
    username: "user"
    password: "pass"
    registry: "quay.io"
    fromSecret: "secret-key" # Only if using credentials from secret
  storage:
    enabled: true
    url: "minio_url"
    secretKey: "minio_secret_key"
    accessID: "minio_access_id"
    bucket: "bucket"
    path: "/bucket/path"
    fromSecret: "secret-Key" # Only if using credentials from secrets
  repository: 
    url: "https://github.com/mocaccinoOS/mocaccino-extra"
    path: "/foo/path"
    checkout: "hash_or_branch"
  options:
    pull: true
    clean: true
    onlyTarget: true
    full: true
    all: true
    privileged: true
    backend: "buildah"
    compression: "gzip"
    resources:
        requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "200Mi"
        limits:
            cpu: "10m"
            memory: "1Mi"
    push: true
    tree:
    - /tree/path
    noDeps: true
    color: true
    spinner: true
    imageRepository: "quay.io/mocaccinocache/extra-amd64-cache"
```

If storage and registry credentials are sourced from secrets, the secret should have the following fields and live in the same namespace of the workload:

```yaml
storageUrl: ""
storageSecretKey: ""
storageAccessID: ""
registryUri: ""
registryPassword: ""
registryUsername: ""
```

### Backends

`options.backend` selects the build backend passed to luet. The default is now
`buildah`. `img` is still accepted but deprecated: luet resolves it to the
buildah backend, so a resource that asks for `img` gets a buildah build.
`docker` and `docker-sidecar` are also available.

### Rootless builds

Builds run unprivileged as uid 1000. Rootless buildah calls
`unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, which a default seccomp profile blocks, so the build
pod needs an unconfined seccomp profile. The controller sets this on the pod it
creates, both as the container `seccompProfile` and as the pre-1.19 annotation
for older clusters.

The AppArmor annotation needs no equivalent field: Kubernetes translates it into
`securityContext.appArmorProfile` automatically, confirmed on 1.31. The seccomp
annotation gets no such translation, because that form was removed in 1.25,
which is why the `seccompProfile` field is set explicitly.

This has been exercised end to end on a kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.31): the
build pod is admitted, and rootless buildah runs a multi-stage build as uid 1000
inside it.

### Extraction needs uid 0, so most packages need `privileged: true`

The *build* runs unprivileged. What follows it may not.

After the backend finishes, luet extracts the built image to produce the package
artifact, and that extraction restores file ownership by calling `lchown` to UID
0. uid 1000 cannot do that, so any package whose contents must be chowned fails
after a completely successful build:

    SUCCESS   Building image luet/cache:49d525a5... done
    ERROR     Error met while extracting image: failed to Lchown
              ".../img" for UID 0, GID 0: operation not permitted

Setting `options.privileged: true` makes the build container run as uid 0 and
the same build completes, producing the artifact. Both outcomes were observed on
the kind cluster above, on the same package, differing only by that flag.

This is not a property of the buildah backend. Extraction happens inside luet
after the backend has already succeeded, so it applies whatever backend built
the image. It was simply not visible until the migration was exercised on a
cluster.

If your package's files are all owned by the build user, extraction has nothing
to chown and the unprivileged path works. Otherwise set `privileged: true`, as
`manifests/example-foo.yaml` does.

The build pod cannot run in a namespace enforcing the `baseline` or `restricted`
Pod Security Standards. Verified on Kubernetes 1.31, a `baseline` namespace
rejects it with:

    violates PodSecurity "baseline:latest":
      forbidden AppArmor profiles (container "spec-build" ... "Unconfined")
      seccompProfile (container "spec-build" must not set
        securityContext.seccompProfile.type to "Unconfined")

Both are required for rootless buildah, which calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`.
Clearing `options.privileged` does not help, because neither violation comes
from `privileged`.

Note that `procMount: Unmasked`, which the controller also sets on the build
container, is **not** among the reasons. `ProcMountType` is a beta feature gate
that is disabled by default, so on a stock cluster the API server silently
stores `procMount: Default` and the setting has no effect. It would become a
third violation on a cluster that enables the gate.

The `vfs` storage driver is used because overlay-on-overlay does not work inside
a pod without `/dev/fuse`. It is materially slower than `overlay`, and anyone
building large images will notice.

The controller image must ship a `buildah` binary. That is installed by a
separate change to the `Dockerfile`; without it the controller runs a build
command for a binary the image does not contain.

None of this has been verified on a real Kubernetes cluster. The test suite
asserts the generated pod spec and the build command strings only. It cannot
show that a kubelet accepts the pod or that a rootless buildah build completes
in one.

## Uninstall

First delete all the workload from the cluster, by deleting all the `packagebuild` resources.

Then run:

```bash

$ kubectl delete -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mudler/luet-k8s/master/hack/kube.yaml

```

build: pkg/generated
	go build

pkg/generated:
	go generate

run: build
	kubectl apply -f manifests/crd.yaml
	kubectl apply -f manifests/example-foo.yaml
	./luet-k8s

module github.com/mudler/luet-k8s

go 1.13

//replace github.com/googleapis/gnostic => github.com/google/gnostic v0.3.1

require (
	github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 v5.4.2
	github.com/google/go-containerregistry v0.7.0
	github.com/mudler/luet v0.0.0-20211228210804-80bc5429bc4a
	github.com/rancher/lasso v0.0.0-20210616224652-fc3ebd901c08
	github.com/rancher/wrangler v0.8.3
	github.com/sirupsen/logrus v1.8.1
	k8s.io/api v0.21.0
	k8s.io/apimachinery v0.21.0
	k8s.io/client-go v0.21.0
	sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime v0.9.0-beta.0
)

FROM golang as builder

ADD . /luet-k8s
RUN cd /luet-k8s && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build

# luet is built from source at a pinned commit and overwrites the released
# binary further down. The buildah backend this controller depends on is merged
# on luet master but is in no tagged release, so install.sh alone yields a luet
# that rejects "--backend buildah" with "invalid backend. Unsupported".
#
# Pinning to a commit also makes the shipped luet reproducible, which
# install.sh plus "luet upgrade" never was.
#
# golang:1.25 because luet's go.mod requires go 1.25.0.
FROM golang:1.25 as luet-builder

# Defaults to master so the image tracks luet as it moves. Override to pin:
#   docker build --build-arg LUET_REF=v0.37.0 .
#   docker build --build-arg LUET_REF=3c30c085ce2f712c9afb00d7b5e0e41824a027ff .
ARG LUET_REF=master

# This ADD is what makes tracking a branch actually work. Without it the RUN
# below is layer-cached and a rebuild silently reuses a stale clone, so "master"
# would freeze at whatever it was the first time the image was built. The
# GitHub API response changes whenever the ref moves, which invalidates the
# cache exactly when there is something new to fetch.
ADD https://api.github.com/repos/mudler/luet/commits/${LUET_REF} /tmp/luet-ref.json

RUN git clone https://github.com/mudler/luet /luet-src \
    && cd /luet-src \
    && git checkout ${LUET_REF} \
    && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build \
        -ldflags "-X 'github.com/mudler/luet/cmd.Version=$(git -C /luet-src describe --always --tags)' \
                  -X 'github.com/mudler/luet/cmd.BuildTime=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z')'" \
        -o /out/luet

FROM ubuntu:24.04
ADD . /luet-k8s
RUN apt-get update
ENV LUET_YES=true
ENV LUET_DEBUG=true
# buildah replaces genuinetools/img as luet's daemonless build backend. It is
# not available on ubuntu 20.04 at all, which is why this base moved to 24.04.
RUN apt-get install -y uidmap curl wget git libcap2-bin buildah
RUN curl https://luet.io/install.sh | sh
RUN chmod u-s /usr/bin/new[gu]idmap && \
    setcap cap_setuid+eip /usr/bin/newuidmap && \
    setcap cap_setgid+eip /usr/bin/newgidmap 
# ubuntu 24.04 ships a default 'ubuntu' user occupying uid 1000, which this
# image needs: builds run unprivileged as uid 1000 in the workload pod.
RUN userdel -r ubuntu 2>/dev/null || true
RUN useradd -u 1000 -d /luet -ms /bin/bash luet
RUN luet upgrade && luet install repository/mocaccino-extra && luet install net-fs/minio-client container/docker

# Overwrite the released luet with the pinned source build, AFTER the package
# installs above. install.sh is still what provisions /etc/luet (base config,
# repos.conf.d, config.protect.d), which a bare source build does not create,
# and the installs need a working luet. Copying last guarantees the pinned
# binary is the one that ships, with nothing able to replace it afterwards.
COPY --from=luet-builder /out/luet /usr/bin/luet

RUN mkdir -p /run/runc  && chmod 777 /run/runc

USER luet
WORKDIR /luet
COPY --from=builder /luet-k8s/luet-k8s /usr/bin/luet-k8s
RUN chmod -R 777 /luet
ENTRYPOINT "/usr/bin/luet-k8s"

apiVersion: build.luet.io/v1alpha1
kind: PackageBuild
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  packageName: container/img
  repository:
    url: "https://github.com/mocaccinoOS/mocaccino-extra"
  storage:
    enabled: false
    url: "minio_endpoint"
    secretKey: ""
    accessID: ""
    bucket: ""
    path: ""
  options:
    #pull: true
      #imageRepository: ""

    # Paths are relative to the checked out repository. This package's build
    # steps interpolate {{.Values.arch}}, so without a values file the URL it
    # fetches renders as "img-linux-<no value>" and the build fails.
    values:
      - /values/amd64.yaml

    # Required for this package, and for any package whose artifact extraction
    # has to change file ownership. Extraction runs inside luet after the build
    # backend has finished, and chowns to UID 0, which the default uid 1000
    # cannot do. Without it the build fails with:
    #
    #   failed to Lchown "..." for UID 0, GID 0: operation not permitted
    #
    # See the "Rootless builds" section of the README.
    privileged: true

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: luet-k8s
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: luet-k8s
  namespace: luet-k8s
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: luet-k8s
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - build.luet.io
  resources:
  - packagebuilds/status
  - repobuilds/status
  verbs:
  - create
  - delete
  - patch
  - update
- apiGroups:
  - build.luet.io
  resources:
  - packagebuilds
  - repobuilds
  verbs:
  - create
  - delete
  - get
  - list
  - patch
  - update
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  verbs:
  - create
  - delete
  - get
  - list
  - update
  - watch

- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - events
  verbs:
  - create


---
apiVersion: v1
kind: List
items:
  - apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
    kind: ClusterRoleBinding
    metadata:
      name: luet-k8s
    subjects:
    - kind: ServiceAccount
      name: luet-k8s
      namespace: luet-k8s
    roleRef:
      kind: ClusterRole
      name: luet-k8s
      apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: controller
  name: controller
  namespace: luet-k8s
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: controller
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: controller
      name: controller
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: luet-k8s
      containers:
        - name: controller
          image: "quay.io/mudler/luet-k8s-controller:latest"
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          command: ["/usr/bin/luet-k8s"]

apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: packagebuilds.build.luet.io
spec:
  group: build.luet.io
  version: v1alpha1
  names:
    kind: PackageBuild
    plural: packagebuilds
  scope: Namespaced
  subresources:
    status: {}

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: docker-api-master
  labels:
    app: docker-api-master
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: docker-api-master
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: docker-api-master
      name: docker-api-master   
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: dind
          image: docker:19.03-dind
          command:
            - dockerd
            - '--mtu=1250'
            - '--host=tcp://0.0.0.0:2375'
          env:
            - name: DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR
              value: ""
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 500Mi
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /lib/modules
              name: modules
              readOnly: true
            - mountPath: /sys/fs/cgroup
              name: cgroup
            - name: dind-storage
              mountPath: /var/lib/docker
      volumes:
        - name: modules
          hostPath:
            path: /lib/modules
            type: Directory
        - name: cgroup
          hostPath:
            path: /sys/fs/cgroup
            type: Directory
        - name: dind-storage
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: docker
spec:
  selector:
    app: docker-api-master
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 2375
      targetPort: 2375
  topologyKeys:
    - "kubernetes.io/hostname"

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:

  labels:

spec:
